source.title: C3T: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning for Sentiment Shifts in Social-Media Conversation Trees

confidence_rationale: PREPRINT, verified on arXiv (2609.02131, submitted 2026-09-02); the thought's citation is exact. Banked as a METHODOLOGICAL anchor only, which is what the chip specifies and what the thought itself concedes -- its findings do not transfer to embodied agents. What is transferable is the shape of the attribution problem: the model treats discourse moves (denial/correction, evidence, toxicity) as candidate INTERVENTIONS, learns sparse ancestor attribution over a conversation tree to identify which prior message drove a reply, and supports counterfactual queries by forcing intervention embeddings on or off. Direction 'unknown' and confidence 0.3 deliberately: the paper bears on HOW one would test an other-agent-caused hypothesis, not on whether REE needs one. Sentiment attribution in rumour threads is not other-agent causal-model selection.
failure_signatures: INV-102 requires a distinct OTHER-agent-caused hypothesis alongside world-caused and self-caused. C3T shows the attribution can be posed and estimated when the candidate causes are DISCRETE, LABELLED discourse moves in an explicit tree. REE has neither the labels nor the tree; if an REE implementation needs an annotated intervention vocabulary to make ancestor attribution tractable, that is a substantive cost this paper hides rather than solves.

The counterfactual here is implemented by toggling an intervention embedding in a learned model, not by intervening on the world. A REE evaluation using the same device would be measuring its own model's sensitivity, not the causal structure of its environment -- which is exactly the confound INV-102's falsifier has to avoid.

mapping.source_claim_statement: C3T models discourse moves in rumour-focused conversation threads (denial/correction, evidence/link, toxicity/attack) as candidate interventions, over a causally annotated dataset layer (CaSiRe) providing sentiment labels, parent-child shift indicators, intervention tags and explicit causal-source annotations. It learns sparse ancestor attribution to identify which prior messages plausibly drove a reply's sentiment and supports counterfactual queries by forcing intervention embeddings on or off. Denials, corrections and evidence reduce downstream negativity while toxicity increases it; attribution is reported as more reliable than open-weight LLM approaches.
mapping.ree_translation: INV-102 says causal-model selection must include an other-agent-caused hypothesis; MECH-430 says provenance is a source VECTOR including source identity, not a single bit. C3T is a worked example of estimating WHICH other agent's prior act caused an observed change, with competing candidate causes and counterfactual tests -- the methodological shape both claims imply. It is not evidence for either.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Text sentiment in social-media threads, with human-annotated intervention labels and an explicit parent-child tree given in advance. An embodied agent has no annotated intervention vocabulary and must infer the tree; the thought itself states the findings do not transfer. Counterfactuals are toggles on a learned embedding, not interventions on the world. Preprint.
mapping.source_context: NLP; rumour conversation threads with the CaSiRe causal annotation layer.

confidence_components.notes: Deliberately floored. Direction 'unknown' because a methodology paper in a distant domain cannot bear on the truth of either claim; the entry exists so the citation is verified and its limits recorded.
